**What I found (all evidence is `path:line` from the pinned tree at `74ed789f`)**

The candidate is the same "insecure temporary files" class that Passenger fixed twice before (`NEWS:536-557`), and the pinned tree still contains several independent, unguarded temp-file sites:

| Trap | Site | Mechanism | Why a solver would dismiss it |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `bin/passenger-install-nginx-module:548` fixed `/tmp/passenger-check.c` + gcc-produced `.o`, no `O_EXCL` | M2 (hand-rolled second implementation of the guarded compile probe; `utils/tmpio` is even required at line 43) | one-line `#include`, output to `/dev/null`, both files unlinked in `ensure` |
| T2 | `PlatformInfo.tmpexedir` (`platform_info.rb:245-268`, duplicated at 271-291) writes + executes `$TMPDIR/test-exe.<pid>.<object_id>` | M4 | content is a fixed `#!/bin/sh` line, chmod 0700 before exec, unlinked, memoized |
| T3 | HelperAgent `FileBackedPipe("/tmp")` (`RequestHandler.h:304,311`; `FileBackedPipe.h:265-271,351`) buffers request bodies to `buffer.<pid>.<ptr>` with `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC` | M1 (same sink as the Ruby `TeeInput`/`TmpIO`, different entry point) | unlinked right after open, dir is a constructor arg, name has a heap pointer |
| T4 | `Utils.passenger_tmpdir` (`utils/tmpdir.rb:47,57-59`) creates `/tmp/passenger.1.0.<pid>` + `backends` with `u=rwxs,g=rwx,o=rwx` (0777) via `mkdir -p -m` | M4 | comment says test-only; loaders replace it with the secure generation dir (`rack-preloader.rb:84`) |
| T5 | Standalone nginx config: `mktmpdir` then `chmod 0755` (`command.rb:192`), config `0644` (`:219`) carrying `union_station_key` (`config.erb:126-129`) | M11 coupled value | workers started with `--user` must read it |
| T6 | Crash log `/var/tmp/passenger-crash-log.<time_t>` (fallback `/tmp`) opened `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC` 0600 without `O_EXCL` (`Base.cpp:773-786`) | M4 | crash-only, timestamped, 0600 |
| T7 | `PlatformInfo` disk cache `File.open(cache,"wb")` (`platform_info.rb:101-106`) | M4 | build-only dir (`build/basics.rb:127`), same-user |

`independent_groups` = 7 (T2 and T7 share a file but not a fix site). Recommended design: **T1+T2+T3+T4+T5** (deepseek-shaped T1-T4, coupled-value/mimo T5), with T6/T7 excluded because their crash-only/build-only reachability would force contrived hidden tests.

**Caveat recorded in `unverified`:** I could not read the actual fix commits `34b1087870c2` / `94428057c602` (git objects are outside the permitted read root, Bash disabled), so which site the B advisory names — and therefore the `advisory_route` origin labels and `b_in_code_a_wrote` — are inferred from the code and from the advisory surface described in `NEWS`, not observed. `usable: true`, effort ≈120 min.
